sentences.en: And he started tinkering around with cement and with concrete and figuring out different ways to, you know, to perfect the mix.
sentences.zh: 去写那些听起来像是世界上最无聊的东西？

sentences.en: And eventually, literally through tinkering in his backyard, he came up with the idea of reinforced concrete,
sentences.zh: 原因在于，沙子实际上是地球上最重要的固体物质。

sentences.en: which is concrete with those steel bars running through it.
sentences.zh: 它是现代文明真正的基石。

sentences.en: And that was Ernest Ransom's great innovation.
sentences.zh: 而那正是欧内斯特·兰瑟姆的伟大创新。

sentences.en: Basically, he found that by putting steel bars inside the concrete, the concrete would bind to those bars,
sentences.zh: 基本上，他发现通过在混凝土中加入钢筋，混凝土会与这些钢筋结合，

sentences.en: and it would massively increase the tensile strength of the concrete.
sentences.zh: 从而极大地提高混凝土的抗拉强度。

sentences.en: And he realized, wow, this is an incredible building material.
sentences.zh: 他意识到，哇，这是一种不可思议的建筑材料。

sentences.en: I can build the walls and the roofs of structures with this stuff, and it'll be cheap, and it'll be strong.
sentences.zh: 我可以用这种材料建造墙壁和屋顶，既便宜又坚固。

sentences.en: And holy smokes, this is the material of the future, thought Ernest Ransom.
sentences.zh: 欧内斯特·兰瑟姆心想，天哪，这就是未来的材料。

sentences.en: So he ran around the country trying to sell people on this idea, and basically, people laughed at him.
sentences.zh: 于是他四处奔走，试图向人们推销这个想法，但基本上，人们都在嘲笑他。

sentences.en: They were just like, why in the world would we even try this crazy new building material?
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，我们为什么要尝试这种疯狂的新建筑材料呢？

sentences.en: We build with stone, we build with bricks, we build with timber.
sentences.zh: 我们一直用石头、砖块和木材盖房子。

sentences.en: These things have been tried and trusted for centuries.
sentences.zh: 这些材料已经经过了几个世纪的考验，值得信赖。

sentences.en: Why on earth would we take a chance on your wacky new idea?
sentences.zh: 我们凭什么要冒险尝试你那古怪的新点子？

sentences.en: So he literally tries for years and years to sell people on this idea, and he gets a few commissions.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实尝试了多年，试图向人们推销这个想法，也确实接到了一些订单。

sentences.en: He manages to build a few, get a few buildings built out of concrete in a couple of different places,
sentences.zh: 他设法在几个不同的地方用混凝土建造了几座建筑，

sentences.en: two or three of them in San Francisco where he lives.
sentences.zh: 其中两三座就在他居住的旧金山。

sentences.en: So then comes 1906, the great San Francisco earthquake.
sentences.zh: 然后就到了1906年，旧金山大地震。

sentences.en: Massive earthquake, demolishes most of the city, followed by an enormous fire that basically burns San Francisco to the ground.
sentences.zh: 那是一场大地震，摧毁了大部分城市，随之而来的大火几乎将旧金山夷为平地。

sentences.en: But when the smoke clears and the dust is settled, some of the very few structures left standing in San Francisco are Ernest Ransom's reinforced concrete buildings.
sentences.zh: 但当烟雾散去、尘埃落定后，旧金山极少数幸存下来的建筑中，就有欧内斯特·兰瑟姆的钢筋混凝土建筑。

sentences.en: And that was a real turning point.
sentences.zh: 那是一个真正的转折点。

sentences.en: People all around the country, and in fact, all around the world, looked at that and said, wow, that concrete stuff, that really works.
sentences.zh: 全国乃至全世界的人们看到这一幕都说，哇，那种混凝土材料真的很管用。

sentences.en: You know, it withstood the earthquake, it withstood the fire.
sentences.zh: 你看，它经受住了地震，也经受住了火灾。

sentences.en: That stuff looks great.
sentences.zh: 那东西看起来真棒。

sentences.en: And in your book, you talk about how the new concrete industry that was developing really took advantage of these images from the San Francisco fire
sentences.zh: 在你的书中，你谈到了当时正在发展的新兴混凝土行业是如何利用旧金山大火的这些影像，

sentences.en: and the concrete warehouses that survived as a way to argue that, like, hey, check out this amazing new fire-safe and earthquake-proof material.
sentences.zh: 以及那些幸存下来的混凝土仓库，来证明这是一种了不起的防火防震新材料。

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: They pushed themselves, you know, to builders, to engineers, to the general public in a really big way,
sentences.zh: 他们确实在大力向建筑商、工程师和公众推广自己，

sentences.en: advertising themselves really as the, you know, the material of the future.
sentences.zh: 把自己宣传为未来的材料。

sentences.en: And in fact, it is.
sentences.zh: 事实上也确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, concrete is an amazingly versatile and useful material.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，混凝土是一种用途极其广泛且实用的材料。

sentences.en: It's very easy to work with.
sentences.zh: 它非常易于使用。

sentences.en: It's cheap, and it's really strong, as long as you build it correctly.
sentences.zh: 只要施工得当，它既便宜又非常坚固。

sentences.en: But you can see it.
sentences.zh: 但你可以看得出来。

sentences.en: I mean, I sort of trawled through a lot of newspapers at the time.
sentences.zh: 我当时查阅了大量的报纸。

sentences.en: And, I mean, it was almost like, you know, computers and digital technology in the 90s,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那感觉就像90年代的计算机和数字技术一样，

sentences.en: just the way that journalists were writing about this stuff.
sentences.zh: 记者们写这些东西的方式如出一辙。

sentences.en: It's just like, oh, amazing.
sentences.zh: 就像是，哦，太神奇了。

sentences.en: Science has revolutionized our way of building.
sentences.zh: 科学彻底改变了我们的建筑方式。

sentences.en: Nevermore will we have to worry about fire.
sentences.zh: 我们再也不用担心火灾了。

sentences.en: Like, you know, as though concrete was going to solve every problem known to man.
sentences.zh: 就好像混凝土能解决人类已知的所有问题一样。

sentences.en: It was really, people were just ecstatic over it.
sentences.zh: 人们当时确实对它狂热不已。

sentences.en: And in fact, Thomas Edison, he was just in love with concrete.
sentences.zh: 事实上，托马斯·爱迪生就对混凝土情有独钟。

sentences.en: He thought concrete was going to be, you know, was not only going to be an important building material,
sentences.zh: 他认为混凝土不仅会成为一种重要的建筑材料，

sentences.en: but that basically you could build anything out of concrete.
sentences.zh: 而且基本上任何东西都可以用混凝土建造。

sentences.en: He built several completely all concrete houses in which he furnished with concrete furniture.
sentences.zh: 他建造了几座完全由混凝土构成的房子，并用混凝土家具进行装饰。

sentences.en: He even built a concrete piano that he sent touring around the country.
sentences.zh: 他甚至造了一架混凝土钢琴，还在全国巡回展出。

sentences.en: It does actually allow architects to be quite inventive because of its, you know, its ability to be shaped in all different kinds of ways.
sentences.zh: 它确实让建筑师能够发挥创造力，因为它能够被塑造成各种各样的形状。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, you look at things, structures like the Guggenheim or, you know, the Sydney Opera House,
sentences.zh: 你看，像古根海姆博物馆或悉尼歌剧院这样的建筑，

sentences.en: these, you know, incredibly fanciful and beautiful creations.
sentences.zh: 这些令人难以置信的奇思妙想和美丽的创造。

sentences.en: You couldn't make those things out of bricks, you know, or stone.
sentences.zh: 你不可能用砖块或石头做出这些东西。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No, concrete is, you know, in addition to making it easy to build really strong, durable structures,
sentences.zh: 不，混凝土，除了能轻松建造出非常坚固耐用的结构外，

sentences.en: it makes it possible to build some of the most beautiful and inventive structures in the world.
sentences.zh: 它还使建造世界上一些最美丽、最具创造力的建筑成为可能。

sentences.en: Not to mention the most useful, I mean, things like, you know, these enormous dams that really made possible the modern Southwest in a lot of ways.
sentences.zh: 更不用说它最实用的用途了，比如那些巨大的水坝，在很多方面成就了现代美国西南部。

sentences.en: And so we went through, in the Western world, we went through our phase of building a lot of concrete in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 所以，在20世纪，西方世界经历了一个大量使用混凝土建造的阶段。

sentences.en: And now there's a huge growth in cities in Asia and Africa.
sentences.zh: 而现在，亚洲和非洲的城市正在飞速增长。

sentences.en: So is that where a lot of the sand is going today?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是今天大部分沙子流向的地方吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So we, I mean, we're still building, of course, in the Western world.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们当然还在建设，

sentences.en: We still use a lot of sand and a lot of concrete here, but it is absolutely dwarfed.
sentences.zh: 我们这里仍然使用大量的沙子和混凝土，但与发展中国家相比，这简直是小巫见大巫。

sentences.en: The amounts that we use in the Western world is absolutely dwarfed by what's going on in the developing world.
sentences.zh: 我们在西方世界使用的数量与发展中国家正在发生的事情相比，完全被掩盖了。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is, number one, there's more and more people in the world all the time, right?
sentences.zh: 原因在于，第一，世界上的人口越来越多，对吧？

sentences.en: Population's growing.
sentences.zh: 人口在增长。

sentences.en: And more and more of them are moving into cities all the time.
sentences.zh: 而且越来越多的人一直在涌入城市。

sentences.en: The same thing that happened in this country a hundred years ago.
sentences.zh: 这和一百年前在这个国家发生的事情一样。

sentences.en: People left the agricultural countryside.
sentences.zh: 人们离开了农业乡村。

sentences.en: They left farming villages and moved into cities.
sentences.zh: 他们离开了农耕村庄，搬进了城市。

sentences.en: Well, the same thing is happening in India, in China, all over Africa, but on a much bigger scale and in a much faster rate in a much more compressed timeframe.
sentences.zh: 同样的事情正在印度、中国和整个非洲发生，但规模更大，速度更快，时间跨度也更紧凑。

sentences.en: So to give you an idea, we're adding the equivalent of eight New York cities to the world every single year.
sentences.zh: 为了让你有个概念，我们每年向世界增加的建筑量相当于八个纽约市。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Here's another way to think about it.
sentences.zh: 还有另一种思考方式。

sentences.en: The amount of concrete that we use every single year is enough to build a wall 88 feet high, 88 feet wide, right around the equator every year.
sentences.zh: 我们每年使用的混凝土总量足以建造一堵88英尺高、88英尺宽的墙，环绕赤道一周。

sentences.en: And most of that is happening in the developing world.
sentences.zh: 而其中大部分都发生在发展中国家。

sentences.en: And more than anywhere else, it's happening in China.
sentences.zh: 而且比任何地方都多，它发生在中国。

sentences.en: China is far and away the world's number one consumer of sand and of concrete.
sentences.zh: 中国是世界上遥遥领先的沙子和混凝土消费国。

sentences.en: Hundreds of millions of people in China have moved from the countryside into cities in the last decade or two.
sentences.zh: 在过去的一二十年里，中国有数亿人从农村搬到了城市。

sentences.en: And remember, of course, cities are made of concrete.
sentences.zh: 记住，城市是由混凝土构成的。

sentences.en: And so where is China's sand coming from?
sentences.zh: 那么中国的沙子是从哪里来的呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So the thing with sand is you always want to get it from somewhere close to where you're going to actually use it because sand is very heavy.
sentences.zh: 关于沙子，你总是希望从离使用地点近的地方获取，因为沙子非常重。

sentences.en: A cubic yard of sand weighs more than a ton.
sentences.zh: 一立方码的沙子重量超过一吨。

sentences.en: So if you have to transport it more than a few miles, the cost of it goes up very quickly.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你必须运输超过几英里，成本就会迅速上升。

sentences.en: So basically, builders in China and everywhere else are always looking for sand that's close by.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，中国和其他地方的建筑商总是在寻找附近的沙子。

sentences.en: So think about Shanghai, for example.
sentences.zh: 以上海为例。

sentences.en: Shanghai is one of these cities that has just exploded in the last 20 years.
sentences.zh: 上海就是过去20年里迅速扩张的城市之一。

sentences.en: More skyscrapers have been built in Shanghai in the last 20 years than there are in all of New York City.
sentences.zh: 过去20年里上海建造的摩天大楼比整个纽约市还要多。

sentences.en: So obviously, they are using just a staggering amount of sand.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，他们使用的沙子数量惊人。

sentences.en: Where is it all coming from?
sentences.zh: 这一切都从哪里来？

sentences.en: Well, in the early part of this century, they were getting most of it from the Yangtze River.
sentences.zh: 在本世纪初，他们大部分是从长江获取的。

sentences.en: They were just scooping it right off the bottom of the Yangtze River.
sentences.zh: 他们直接从长江底部挖沙。

sentences.en: And that caused a lot of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这导致了很多问题。

sentences.en: Number one, it was causing riverbanks to literally collapse, right?
sentences.zh: 第一，它导致河岸直接坍塌，对吧？

sentences.en: When you dig out the middle of the river, the sides of the river often just collapse, taking with it agricultural land, villages.
sentences.zh: 当你挖出河床中心时，河岸往往会直接坍塌，带走农田和村庄。

sentences.en: You know, it snarls up shipping in a really terrible way.
sentences.zh: 它以一种非常糟糕的方式阻碍了航运。

sentences.en: And it also does serious damage to the river's ecosystem.
sentences.zh: 它也对河流的生态系统造成了严重破坏。

sentences.en: Anything that was living on the bottom of the river obviously is gone.
sentences.zh: 任何生活在河底的东西显然都消失了。

sentences.en: Their habitat's just been destroyed.
sentences.zh: 它们的栖息地被彻底摧毁了。

sentences.en: And also, when you silt up the water like that, it blocks the sunlight from reaching plants that are growing underneath the water.
sentences.zh: 而且，当你把水搅得浑浊时，它会阻挡阳光到达水下生长的植物。

sentences.en: So huge, huge damage.
sentences.zh: 所以破坏非常巨大。

sentences.en: And the Chinese authorities realized this.
sentences.zh: 中国当局意识到了这一点。

sentences.en: They were like, whoa, this is a serious problem for the Yangtze River, which is an incredibly important resource for China.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得，哇，这对长江来说是一个严重的问题，长江对中国来说是一个极其重要的资源。

sentences.en: It's the source of drinking water for hundreds of millions of people, fish, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: 它是数亿人的饮用水源，还有鱼类等等。

sentences.en: So they had to ban sand mining on the Yangtze River.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不得不禁止在长江采砂。

sentences.en: As a result, sand miners just sort of pushed their operations a few dozen miles upstream to the biggest freshwater lake in China.
sentences.zh: 结果，采砂者只是把作业地点向上游移动了几十英里，到了中国最大的淡水湖。

sentences.en: It's called Lake Poyang.
sentences.zh: 它叫鄱阳湖。

sentences.en: So Lake Poyang has now become the biggest sand mine in the world.
sentences.zh: 所以鄱阳湖现在成了世界上最大的采砂场。

sentences.en: It's about 230-odd million tons of sand are scooped out of this lake every year.
sentences.zh: 每年从这个湖里挖出大约2.3亿多吨沙子。

sentences.en: And that now, of course, is starting to generate its own set of environmental probleMs.
sentences.zh: 当然，这现在也开始产生它自己的一系列环境问题。

sentences.en: It's causing real damage to the many, many fish and birds that live there, including endangered species like freshwater porpoises.
sentences.zh: 它对那里生活的许多鱼类和鸟类造成了真正的伤害，包括江豚等濒危物种。

sentences.en: So basically, where does China get its sand from?
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，中国从哪里获取沙子？

sentences.en: It gets it from wherever is handy.
sentences.zh: 它从任何方便的地方获取。

sentences.en: And when you put that much pressure on whatever river or lake or whatever is handy, it causes problems inevitably.
sentences.zh: 当你对任何河流、湖泊或任何方便的地方施加如此大的压力时，不可避免地会引起问题。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, is this a race to the bottom?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一场逐底竞争吗？

sentences.en: Are we just going to run out of sand?
sentences.zh: 我们是不是快没沙子用了？

sentences.en: So we're not going to completely run out of sand any time in the foreseeable future.
sentences.zh: 在可预见的未来，我们不会完全用完沙子。

sentences.en: We're not going to be fighting over the very last little pile of the last few grains on Earth.
sentences.zh: 我们不会为了地球上最后一点沙粒而争斗。

sentences.en: But what's happening with sand is much more like what's happening with oil and gas, right?
sentences.zh: 但沙子的情况更像是石油和天然气的情况，对吧？

sentences.en: There's still a lot of it on the planet.
sentences.zh: 地球上仍然有很多。

sentences.en: But the stuff that's easy to get at has been mostly tapped out.
sentences.zh: 但容易获取的部分大部分已经被开采完了。

sentences.en: The stuff that's close to the surface and cheap and easy to get our hands on is increasingly disappearing.
sentences.zh: 那些靠近地表、便宜且容易获取的资源正在日益消失。

sentences.en: And we're having to go further and further and do more and more damage to get at the stuff that's left.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不走得更远，做更多的破坏来获取剩下的资源。

sentences.en: So the same thing that you see happening with oil, where we're having to do things like fracking and offshore oil drilling to get at the oil that's left.
sentences.zh: 所以，就像你在石油行业看到的那样，我们不得不进行水力压裂和海上钻探来获取剩余的石油。

sentences.en: Similar kind of thing is happening with sand.
sentences.zh: 沙子的情况也类似。

sentences.en: We're having to dig deeper and deeper and do more and more damage to get at the dwindling supplies of sand.
sentences.zh: 我们不得不挖得越来越深，做越来越多的破坏来获取日益减少的沙子供应。

sentences.en: Beyond the damage that you can inflict on the land by mining the sand, what is the cost of concrete to the planet?
sentences.zh: 除了开采沙子对土地造成的破坏外，混凝土对地球的代价是什么？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So concrete has some very significant costs.
sentences.zh: 混凝土确实有一些非常沉重的代价。

sentences.en: Number one is carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 第一是碳排放。

sentences.en: So manufacturing cement is, depending on how you measure it, either the second or the third biggest carbon dioxide emitter, greenhouse gas emitter on the planet.
sentences.zh: 制造水泥是地球上第二或第三大二氧化碳排放源，具体取决于你的衡量方式。

sentences.en: The energy that's required, it takes a lot of a lot of energy to incinerate all the lime that you need to make cement, number one.
sentences.zh: 所需的能源，首先，焚烧制造水泥所需的石灰需要大量的能源。

sentences.en: And also the process itself gives off a lot of gases.
sentences.zh: 而且这个过程本身也会释放大量的气体。

sentences.en: So it creates somewhere in the neighborhood of 10% of all greenhouse gases are created by the cement industry.
sentences.zh: 所以它产生的温室气体约占全球总量的10%左右。

sentences.en: And of course, you need cement to make concrete.
sentences.zh: 当然，你需要水泥来制造混凝土。

sentences.en: So that's number one.
sentences.zh: 所以这是第一点。

sentences.en: Number two is that by covering so much ground with concrete, you create in a lot of places what's called the urban heat island effect.
sentences.zh: 第二点是，由于用混凝土覆盖了太多的地面，在很多地方造成了所谓的城市热岛效应。

sentences.en: The sun's heat gets soaked up and held by all that concrete.
sentences.zh: 太阳的热量被所有这些混凝土吸收并保留下来。

sentences.en: The temperature of cities can be raised by as much as 10 or 15 degrees just due to the fact that the concrete is retaining all of that heat.
sentences.zh: 城市温度可能会升高多达10到15度，仅仅是因为混凝土保留了所有这些热量。

sentences.en: And that's obviously a big problem in a world that's getting hotter all the time.
sentences.zh: 在一个气候日益变暖的世界里，这显然是一个大问题。

sentences.en: There's another impact that it can have, which is that it can make flooding worse because for the most part, concrete is not porous, right?
sentences.zh: 它还有另一个影响，那就是它会加剧洪水，因为在大多数情况下，混凝土是不透水的，对吧？

sentences.en: Water flows over it.
sentences.zh: 水会在上面流过。

sentences.en: So, for instance, what happened in the last set of floods in Houston is it made those floods worse because when those rivers overflow their banks,
sentences.zh: 所以，例如，休斯顿最近发生的洪水，情况变得更糟，因为当河流漫过堤岸时，

sentences.en: all that water goes pouring into cities and it has nowhere to go.
sentences.zh: 所有的水都涌入城市，无处可去。

sentences.en: It just flows through the concrete streets of the cities.
sentences.zh: 它只能流过城市里混凝土铺成的街道。

sentences.en: So it can really exacerbate flooding in a really serious way.
sentences.zh: 所以它确实会以非常严重的方式加剧洪水。

sentences.en: Do we need to build with as much concrete as we do?
sentences.zh: 我们需要像现在这样使用这么多混凝土来建造吗？

sentences.en: Uh, no, in a nutshell.
sentences.zh: 嗯，简而言之，不需要。

sentences.en: Um, I mean, listen, we need concrete, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，听着，我们需要混凝土，对吧？

sentences.en: This is not, it's not analogous to oil, right?
sentences.zh: 这并不是，这和石油不一样，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is something that we can actually replace with something cleaner and more sustainable with, with, you know, with solar and wind.
sentences.zh: 石油我们可以用太阳能和风能等更清洁、更可持续的能源来替代。

sentences.en: Concrete is a great building material.
sentences.zh: 混凝土是一种很棒的建筑材料。

sentences.en: It has created safe, durable housing for billions of people the world over who didn't have it 20, 30 years ago.
sentences.zh: 它为全世界数十亿人在过去二三十年里没有安全、耐用住房的人们提供了住所。

sentences.en: That's to the good.
sentences.zh: 这是件好事。

sentences.en: So we need concrete.
sentences.zh: 所以我们需要混凝土。

sentences.en: We got to keep using it.
sentences.zh: 我们必须继续使用它。

sentences.en: But yeah, we could use a lot less of it.
sentences.zh: 但确实，我们可以少用很多。

sentences.en: How could we do that?
sentences.zh: 我们该怎么做呢？

sentences.en: Well, first of all, by figuring out ways to restructure how we live in so that we don't need quite as much infrastructure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，首先，要设法重构我们的生活方式，这样我们就不需要那么多的基础设施了。

sentences.en: Cars being the most obvious example.
sentences.zh: 汽车就是最明显的例子。

sentences.en: But also just by making things smaller.
sentences.zh: 但也可以通过把东西做得更小来实现。

sentences.en: I mean, I was just giving some talks about, about my book in the Netherlands and the size of the hotel rooms that I stayed in would shock any hotel staying American.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我刚在荷兰做了一些关于我那本书的演讲，我住的酒店房间大小会让任何住酒店的美国人感到震惊。

sentences.en: I mean, they are tiny.
sentences.zh: 我是说，它们太小了。

sentences.en: There's room for a bed, a single bed, and a little desk, and a window, and a little sink.
sentences.zh: 里面只有一张床，一张单人床，一个小书桌，一扇窗户，还有一个小洗手池。

sentences.en: And that's it, right?
sentences.zh: 就这些，对吧？

sentences.en: There, I mean, you could literally fit two or three of these rooms in the average motel six room.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你完全可以在一个普通的汽车旅馆房间里塞进两三个这样的房间。

sentences.en: You know, it's kind of shocking when you first walk into a room that size.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你第一次走进那么大的房间时，确实有点震惊。

sentences.en: But really, like, who cares?
sentences.zh: 但说真的，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: I was in most of these towns for one night.
sentences.zh: 我在这些城镇大多只待一晚。

sentences.en: I'd go in, I'd, you know, do a little work on my computer, go to sleep, get up, pack up, and leave.
sentences.zh: 我进去，用电脑处理点工作，睡觉，起床，打包，然后离开。

sentences.en: I didn't need more than, I didn't need more than that amount of space.
sentences.zh: 我不需要，我不需要比那更多的空间。

sentences.en: If you think about all the millions of hotel and motel rooms in this country, we could easily cut many of them in half, you know, or houses.
sentences.zh: 如果你想想这个国家数以百万计的酒店和汽车旅馆房间，我们完全可以把它们中的许多减半，或者想想房子。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, Americans famously, we build giant houses.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你知道，美国人以建造巨大的房子而闻名。

sentences.en: We love to have big, huge, sprawling tract houses.
sentences.zh: 我们喜欢拥有巨大、宽敞的住宅区房屋。

sentences.en: And the size of the average American home, by the way, has nearly doubled just in the last couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，美国普通住宅的面积在过去几十年里几乎翻了一番。

sentences.en: We don't need that much space.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要那么大的空间。

sentences.en: You don't need six bathrooms in your house.
sentences.zh: 你不需要在家里有六个浴室。

sentences.en: We could ease, you know, really, we could easily cut down, you know, create a system of extra taxes or tax incentives or whatever to encourage people to live smaller.
sentences.zh: 我们可以轻松地，真的，我们可以轻松地削减，比如，建立一套额外的税收制度或税收激励措施，或者其他什么方式来鼓励人们住得小一点。

sentences.en: And I submit we would be no less happy living that way.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，那样生活我们并不会感到不快乐。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Are there other materials we could be using?
sentences.zh: 还有其他我们可以使用的材料吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 有。

sentences.en: So that's the other thing.
sentences.zh: 所以这是另一回事。

sentences.en: There is a lot of research going on around the world to come up with other materials that we could use in concrete rather than sand.
sentences.zh: 世界各地正在进行大量的研究，以寻找除了沙子之外可以用于混凝土的其他材料。

sentences.en: So there are people who are looking at using bamboo or shredded plastic or recycled tires, shredded tires, or hemp, actually.
sentences.zh: 所以有人正在研究使用竹子、碎塑料或回收轮胎、碎轮胎，甚至是工业大麻。

sentences.en: There's a thing, there's a product called Hempcrete, which you can actually buy right now.
sentences.zh: 有一种东西，有一种产品叫“大麻混凝土”，你现在就可以买到。

sentences.en: And all those things, I think, help.
sentences.zh: 我认为所有这些都有帮助。

sentences.en: I think they're all to the good.
sentences.zh: 我认为它们都是好事。

sentences.en: I think they should all be encouraged.
sentences.zh: 我认为都应该受到鼓励。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, there's only so far we can go with alternative materials.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，替代材料的作用是有限的。

sentences.en: Because like I said, we use 50 billion tons of sand and gravel every year.
sentences.zh: 因为就像我说的，我们每年使用500亿吨沙子和砾石。

sentences.en: And even if we could replace all that sand with bamboo, where are we going to come up with 50 billion tons of bamboo every year, right?
sentences.zh: 即使我们能用竹子代替所有的沙子，我们每年去哪里找500亿吨竹子呢，对吧？

sentences.en: That would create its own set of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 那会引发另一系列问题。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, I think the real way to think about the sand crisis is to kind of reframe the question.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为思考沙子危机的真正方式是重新定义这个问题。

sentences.en: The question isn't really what's going to happen when we run out of sand.
sentences.zh: 问题不在于沙子用完了会发生什么。

sentences.en: The question is, what's going to happen when we run out of everything?
sentences.zh: 问题在于，当一切都用完了会发生什么？

sentences.en: We shouldn't just be thinking about, like, how can we solve the problem of sand?
sentences.zh: 我们不应该只考虑如何解决沙子的问题。

sentences.en: Because really, it sounds familiar, right?
sentences.zh: 因为说真的，这听起来很耳熟，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that we're using too much fresh water.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们正在消耗过多的淡水。

sentences.en: We know that we're cutting down too many trees.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们正在砍伐过多的树木。

sentences.en: We know we're harvesting too many fish out of the oceans.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们正在从海洋中捕捞过多的鱼类。

sentences.en: We know we're burning too much fossil fuel.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们正在燃烧过多的化石燃料。

sentences.en: And now come to find out we're using too much sand.
sentences.zh: 现在又发现我们正在使用过多的沙子。

sentences.en: Well, to my mind, these are not separate probleMs.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这些并不是孤立的问题。

sentences.en: They're all symptoms of the same problem, which is just that we're consuming too much, right?
sentences.zh: 它们都是同一个问题的症状，那就是我们消耗得太多了，对吧？

sentences.en: The way that we live here in the Western world and that lifestyle that we've now exported to the rest of the world,
sentences.zh: 我们在西方世界的生活方式，以及我们现在输出到世界其他地方的那种生活方式，

sentences.en: it just consumes way too many natural resources.
sentences.zh: 消耗了太多的自然资源。

sentences.en: And the planet simply can't sustain it.
sentences.zh: 而地球根本无法支撑。

sentences.en: Now, I think we're going to hit that wall with water sooner than we're going to hit it with sand.
sentences.zh: 现在，我认为我们在水资源方面撞上那堵墙的时间会比沙子更早。

sentences.en: But ultimately, it's the same problem, which is just that the way that we live our lives just isn't sustainable.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，这是同一个问题，即我们的生活方式是不可持续的。

sentences.en: We have got to find ways to build our cities, which is where most human beings now live,
sentences.zh: 我们必须找到建造城市的方法，毕竟大多数人类现在都住在城市里，

sentences.en: in ways that use fewer resources.
sentences.zh: 以减少资源消耗的方式来建造。

sentences.en: That's the only way we're going to avoid total calamity.
sentences.zh: 这是我们避免彻底灾难的唯一途径。

sentences.en: Vince Weiser's book is called The World in a Grain.
sentences.zh: 文斯·威瑟的书叫《沙粒中的世界》。

sentences.en: There is so much more to the story of sand that we didn't even touch on here,
sentences.zh: 关于沙子的故事还有很多，我们在这里甚至还没触及，

sentences.en: including how glass changed civilization.
sentences.zh: 包括玻璃是如何改变文明的。

sentences.en: That's a big deal.
sentences.zh: 那可是件大事。

sentences.en: So if you like this discussion, you'll love the book.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你喜欢这次讨论，你一定会喜欢这本书。

sentences.en: There's a lot of sand locked up in all the concrete in the built world.
sentences.zh: 在建筑世界的所有混凝土中，锁定了大量的沙子。

sentences.en: But there's also a lot of embodied carbon in concrete.
sentences.zh: 但混凝土中也蕴含着大量的隐含碳。

sentences.en: We'll talk about how to quantify that and concrete alternatives after this.
sentences.zh: 稍后我们将讨论如何量化这一点以及混凝土的替代品。

sentences.en: Concrete is the building industry's favorite material.
sentences.zh: 混凝土是建筑业最喜欢的材料。

sentences.en: But it's a problematic fave.
sentences.zh: 但它也是一种令人头疼的宠儿。

sentences.en: And not only because of the global sand crisis.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是因为全球沙子危机。

sentences.en: As Vince Weiser noted, concrete is also extremely carbon intensive.
sentences.zh: 正如文斯·威瑟所指出的，混凝土也是极其耗碳的。

sentences.en: The production of cement, which is the key ingredient in concrete,
sentences.zh: 水泥的生产，也就是混凝土的关键成分，

sentences.en: is responsible for about 8% of the world's CO2 emissions.
sentences.zh: 造成了全球约8%的二氧化碳排放。

sentences.en: And so we thought we'd spend this section of the program
sentences.zh: 所以我们想花这部分节目时间

sentences.en: talking about the climate change impacts of the buildings we create,
sentences.zh: 来谈谈我们建造的建筑物对气候变化的影响，

sentences.en: whether they're made of concrete or wood or some novel material you've never even heard of.
sentences.zh: 无论它们是由混凝土、木材还是你从未听说过的新型材料制成的。

sentences.en: And to do that, I called up Kate Simonen.
sentences.zh: 为了做到这一点，我联系了凯特·西蒙宁。

sentences.en: I'm Kate Simonen, and I'm an architect, instructional engineer,
sentences.zh: 我是凯特·西蒙宁，我是一名建筑师、结构工程师，

sentences.en: and faculty member at the University of Washington.
sentences.zh: 也是华盛顿大学的教员。

sentences.en: And my research is focused on the environmental impact of building materials.
sentences.zh: 我的研究重点是建筑材料对环境的影响。

sentences.en: When we think about the environmental impact of buildings,
sentences.zh: 当我们思考建筑对环境的影响时，

sentences.en: most people really do think about the environmental impact of operating them.
sentences.zh: 大多数人确实会想到它们在运行过程中的环境影响。

sentences.en: The energy cost of operating a building is stuff you probably know.
sentences.zh: 运行建筑物的能源成本是你可能知道的。

sentences.en: All the energy that it takes to heat the building and cool the building and keep the lights on.
sentences.zh: 加热建筑物、冷却建筑物和保持照明所需的所有能源。

sentences.en: But Kate says that when we think about buildings and climate change,
sentences.zh: 但凯特说，当我们思考建筑和气候变化时，

sentences.en: that is not the full picture.
sentences.zh: 那并不是全貌。

sentences.en: There are also the emissions associated with the materials themselves.
sentences.zh: 还有与材料本身相关的排放。

sentences.en: The emissions that were required to make all that concrete and steel and glass.
sentences.zh: 制造所有那些混凝土、钢铁和玻璃所需的排放。

sentences.en: The factories, the steel mills, the trucks that drive around, all of those create emissions.
sentences.zh: 工厂、钢铁厂、四处行驶的卡车，所有这些都会产生排放。

sentences.en: And those emissions are termed the embodied emissions.
sentences.zh: 这些排放被称为隐含排放。

sentences.en: So the emissions that are sort of embodied in the materials,
sentences.zh: 所以这些排放是某种程度上隐含在材料中的，

sentences.en: although they're really the emissions that happened when making the materials.
sentences.zh: 尽管它们实际上是在制造材料时产生的排放。

sentences.en: These emissions are known as embodied carbon,
sentences.zh: 这些排放被称为隐含碳，

sentences.en: the carbon emissions that were needed to create the built environment all around us.
sentences.zh: 即创造我们周围建筑环境所需的碳排放。

sentences.en: Kate heads up the Carbon Leadership Forum at the University of Washington.
sentences.zh: 凯特领导着华盛顿大学的碳领导力论坛。

sentences.en: It's a group of builders and designers and academics working to reduce embodied carbon.
sentences.zh: 这是一个由建筑商、设计师和学者组成的团体，致力于减少隐含碳。

sentences.en: And she says that new materials and greener manufacturing are important for the future.
sentences.zh: 她说，新材料和更环保的制造方式对未来很重要。

sentences.en: But the first thing we can do to reduce embodied carbon
sentences.zh: 但我们减少隐含碳的第一件事

sentences.en: is just to keep using the buildings we've already built.
sentences.zh: 就是继续使用我们已经建好的建筑物。

sentences.en: If we can keep what we have, that's the first best step to reducing embodied carbon.
sentences.zh: 如果我们能保留现有的建筑，这是减少隐含碳的第一步，也是最好的一步。

sentences.en: So renovating buildings and maintaining them is key.
sentences.zh: 所以翻新建筑物并维护它们是关键。

sentences.en: We've invested a lot in that concrete.
sentences.zh: 我们在那些混凝土上投入了很多。

sentences.en: And so let's make our choices correctly when we
sentences.zh: 所以让我们在选择制造新事物以及维护和保留现有事物时，

sentences.en: choose to make new things and maintain and keep the things that we have.
sentences.zh: 做出正确的选择。

sentences.en: But even so, we know there's going to be a building boom in the coming decades.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，我们知道未来几十年将会出现建筑热潮。

sentences.en: We need new housing, new green energy infrastructure, new transportation.
sentences.zh: 我们需要新的住房、新的绿色能源基础设施、新的交通设施。

sentences.en: And if all those structures are being made using traditional steel and concrete,
sentences.zh: 如果所有这些结构都是用传统的钢铁和混凝土建造的，

sentences.en: it is going to be a problem for the climate.
sentences.zh: 那将是一个气候问题。

sentences.en: But Kate says there are a lot of potential low-carbon building materials out there these days,
sentences.zh: 但凯特说，现在有很多潜在的低碳建筑材料，

sentences.en: including alternative concretes and low-carbon steel.
sentences.zh: 包括替代混凝土和低碳钢。

sentences.en: And there's exciting new technologies that are growing rocks
sentences.zh: 还有令人兴奋的新技术，可以通过捕获大气中或烟囱里的碳，

sentences.en: by capturing carbon from the atmosphere or at smokestacks and turning it back into limestone.
sentences.zh: 并将其转化回石灰石来“种植”岩石。

sentences.en: So that if we talk about carbon capture and storage,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我们谈论碳捕集与封存，

sentences.en: think about carbon capture and using that carbon to build buildings with
sentences.zh: 可以考虑碳捕集并利用这些碳来建造建筑物，

sentences.en: so we could take those rocks and turn them into buildings.
sentences.zh: 这样我们就可以把那些岩石变成建筑物。

sentences.en: That kind of carbon capture technology is a long way from becoming a reality.
sentences.zh: 那种碳捕集技术距离成为现实还有很长的路要走。

sentences.en: But one of the most promising green building materials that people are using right now
sentences.zh: 但人们现在正在使用的最有前途的绿色建筑材料之一，

sentences.en: is actually one of the oldest building materials on Earth.
sentences.zh: 实际上是地球上最古老的建筑材料之一。

sentences.en: Wood.
sentences.zh: 木材。

sentences.en: A wooden building stores carbon within it.
sentences.zh: 木制建筑将碳储存在其中。

sentences.en: And so if you can build with more wood instead of concrete,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你能用更多的木材而不是混凝土来建造，

sentences.en: you have the potential to dramatically reduce the embodied carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 你就有可能显著减少隐含碳排放。

sentences.en: You could potentially even have a building that is a net carbon negative.
sentences.zh: 你甚至可能拥有一座净碳负排放的建筑。

sentences.en: And with that goal in mind, architects and engineers are developing
sentences.zh: 怀着这个目标，建筑师和工程师们正在开发

sentences.en: large manufactured wood products that they call mass timber.
sentences.zh: 大型人造木制品，他们称之为“大木材”。

sentences.en: So mass timber is a term that defines wood buildings that are made out of large
sentences.zh: 所以“大木材”是一个定义木结构建筑的术语，这些建筑由大块木材制成，

sentences.en: pieces of wood, so massive pieces of wood.
sentences.zh: 也就是巨大的木块。

sentences.en: You make mass timber products by layering sheets of wood on top of one another
sentences.zh: 你通过将木板一层一层地叠在一起，

sentences.en: and then compressing them to create extremely strong,
sentences.zh: 然后压缩它们来制造极其坚固的预制木板，

sentences.en: prefabricated wood panels that can be assembled into all kinds of structures.
sentences.zh: 这些木板可以组装成各种结构。

sentences.en: Architects are beginning to experiment with using mass timber to build anything
sentences.zh: 建筑师们开始尝试使用大木材来建造各种建筑，

sentences.en: from skyscrapers to bridges.
sentences.zh: 从摩天大楼到桥梁。

sentences.en: And the advantage of mass timber is that the thick pieces of wood
sentences.zh: 大木材的优势在于厚木块具有固有的耐火特性。

sentences.en: have an inherent fire-resistant characteristic to them.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，如果你想生一堆篝火，

sentences.en: So imagine if you're trying to build a campfire
sentences.zh: 你用细小的树枝来生火，

sentences.en: and you make it out of little small sticks,
sentences.zh: 它们很快就会烧光，留下一堆灰烬。

sentences.en: they all burn up and you get a pile of ash.
sentences.zh: 但如果你从非常大的木块开始，

sentences.en: But if you start with really big pieces of wood
sentences.zh: 然后你睡着了，让火自己烧完，

sentences.en: and then you fall asleep and let the fire burn itself out,
sentences.zh: 当你回来时，你的壁炉里仍然有一根木头。

sentences.en: you come back and you still have a log in your fireplace.
sentences.zh: 所以建筑也是一样的情况。

sentences.en: So that's the same thing that happens with buildings.
sentences.zh: 对于重型木结构建筑，它几乎会自行熄灭。

sentences.en: With a heavy timber building, it sort of almost puts itself out.
sentences.zh: 我是说，摩天大楼在火灾中的表现是一回事，

sentences.en: I mean, how a skyscraper behaves in fire is one thing,
sentences.zh: 我是说，摩天大楼在火灾中的表现是一回事，

sentences.en: but it feels strange to think about skyscrapers made of wood at all,
sentences.zh: 但想到用木头建造摩天大楼，总觉得有些奇怪，

sentences.en: you know, like in a modern age.
sentences.zh: 你知道，毕竟现在是现代社会了。

sentences.en: Well, why is anything weird?
sentences.zh: 嗯，为什么会觉得奇怪呢？

sentences.en: Things are just weird because we haven't heard of them.
sentences.zh: 事情之所以奇怪，只是因为我们没听说过而已。

sentences.en: If you went back 150 years, nobody would have heard of a steel building.
sentences.zh: 如果你回到150年前，没人听说过钢结构建筑。

sentences.en: And they were worried about cast iron.
sentences.zh: 当时人们还担心铸铁建筑呢。

sentences.en: So there were cast iron buildings and cast iron melted
sentences.zh: 那时候有铸铁建筑，而铸铁会熔化，

sentences.en: and people were very concerned about it.
sentences.zh: 所以人们对此非常担忧。

sentences.en: So if you, you know, if you look back in time,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你回顾过去，

sentences.en: there's been massive innovations about what we do.
sentences.zh: 我们在建筑方式上已经有了巨大的创新。

sentences.en: And if you look back in time,
sentences.zh: 如果你回顾过去，

sentences.en: there's been massively large, tall wood buildings
sentences.zh: 其实早就有过非常高大的木结构建筑，

sentences.en: that have built and lasted a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 而且它们建成后已经存在了很长一段时间。

sentences.en: So we learn a trade that is handed down to us from other people.
sentences.zh: 我们学习的行业知识是前人传授给我们的。

sentences.en: So a lot of what we learn, we've been told about works.
sentences.zh: 我们学到的很多东西，都是别人告诉我们行之有效的。

sentences.en: And so we have confidence in things because they've been done before.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以对某些事物有信心，是因为它们之前已经被实践过了。

sentences.en: So I don't think it's unreasonable to be a little conservative.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，保持一点保守态度并非不合理。

sentences.en: I mean, we wouldn't want to build a high-rise building
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们肯定不想建造那种

sentences.en: that burns and kills lots of people,
sentences.zh: 会起火并导致多人伤亡的高层建筑，

sentences.en: nor would we want to build a building
sentences.zh: 也不想建造那种

sentences.en: that wasn't able to maintain over a long period of time.
sentences.zh: 无法长期维护的建筑。

sentences.en: You know, if I step back and think,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我退一步思考，

sentences.en: if my driver is climate change,
sentences.zh: 如果我的驱动力是气候变化，

sentences.en: and my driver is climate change,
sentences.zh: 如果我的驱动力是气候变化，

sentences.en: in order to have the building sector
sentences.zh: 为了让建筑行业

sentences.en: be part of the climate solution,
sentences.zh: 成为气候解决方案的一部分，

sentences.en: we're going to have to take some risks.
sentences.zh: 我们就必须承担一些风险。

sentences.en: And so one of the risks will be trying novel materials
sentences.zh: 其中一种风险就是尝试新颖的材料，

sentences.en: and new methods of using those materials
sentences.zh: 以及使用这些材料的新方法，

sentences.en: to drive to a market where we have carbon-negative buildings.
sentences.zh: 从而推动市场实现碳负排放建筑。

sentences.en: Cities full of carbon-negative wooden skyscrapers
sentences.zh: 满是碳负排放木制摩天大楼的城市，

sentences.en: is definitely an attractive vision.
sentences.zh: 绝对是一个诱人的愿景。

sentences.en: And Kate says that wooden buildings
sentences.zh: 凯特说，木制建筑

sentences.en: have the potential to be carbon-negative,
sentences.zh: 确实有潜力实现碳负排放，

sentences.en: but it's not that straightforward.
sentences.zh: 但这并非那么简单。

sentences.en: You have to really analyze every aspect of the supply chain
sentences.zh: 你必须真正分析供应链的每一个环节，

sentences.en: before you can make such a declaration.
sentences.zh: 才能做出这样的声明。

sentences.en: One of the most important things to consider
sentences.zh: 最需要考虑的事情之一，

sentences.en: is where that wood is coming from.
sentences.zh: 就是木材的来源。

sentences.en: Because the forest itself is pulling carbon out of the atmosphere,
sentences.zh: 因为森林本身就在从大气中吸收碳，

sentences.en: and if you take wood out of the forest,
sentences.zh: 如果你从森林中砍伐木材，

sentences.en: you're changing the forest-carbon balance.
sentences.zh: 就会改变森林的碳平衡。

sentences.en: So in order for wood to be a great building material for the climate,
sentences.zh: 所以，要让木材成为气候友好的优质建筑材料，

sentences.en: you have to make sure that it's being harvested sustainably.
sentences.zh: 你必须确保它是以可持续的方式采伐的。

sentences.en: And with wood products, we need to be careful
sentences.zh: 对于木制品，我们需要小心，

sentences.en: that we don't set up a system that incentivizes wasting wood
sentences.zh: 不要建立一套鼓励浪费木材、

sentences.en: and chopping down forests and not replanting them.
sentences.zh: 砍伐森林却不重新种植的制度。

sentences.en: Kate Simonin says that mass timber isn't a perfect building material.
sentences.zh: 凯特·西蒙宁说，重型木材并非完美的建筑材料。

sentences.en: There is no perfect building material.
sentences.zh: 世界上没有完美的建筑材料。

sentences.en: But building stuff always involves difficult choices and trade-offs.
sentences.zh: 但建造任何东西总是涉及艰难的选择和权衡。

sentences.en: And it's Kate's goal to make sure that architects and builders
sentences.zh: 凯特的目标是确保建筑师和建筑商

sentences.en: are considering embodied carbon
sentences.zh: 在决定建造什么以及如何建造时，

sentences.en: when they make their decisions about what to build and how to build it.
sentences.zh: 考虑到隐含碳的问题。

sentences.en: Because we're all going to be living with the consequences.
sentences.zh: 因为我们所有人都要承担相应的后果。

sentences.en: Embodied carbon is up front.
sentences.zh: 隐含碳是预先存在的。

sentences.en: These are the emissions that happen when we build things now.
sentences.zh: 这些排放发生在我们现在建造东西的时候。

sentences.en: We're going to be building a new New York every month until 2050 across the world.
sentences.zh: 到2050年之前，全世界每个月都要新建一个纽约市体量的建筑。

sentences.en: Those emissions are huge.
sentences.zh: 这些排放量是巨大的。

sentences.en: And if we don't figure out how to address them,
sentences.zh: 如果我们不设法解决这些问题，

sentences.en: we're not going to meet climate targets.
sentences.zh: 我们将无法实现气候目标。

sentences.en: So more and more people are recognizing that,

sentences.en: looking for strategies to figure out how to reduce
sentences.zh: 正在寻找策略来设法减少排放，

sentences.zh: 并推动市场转向低碳解决方案。
